tiles.name: PHP2Shell exposure  |  CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619  |  live from OneAgent process technology data
How to read this
tiles.markdown:
**Fix:** PHP 8.5.12 · 8.4.27 · 8.3.36 · 8.2.35. **7.4–8.1:** community source backports only. **Below 7.4:** no fix. Updating is the only complete mitigation.

Tiles are metric queries filtered by the PHP version OneAgent detected on each process (`softwareTechnologies.version`). **Vulnerable = All PHP − Patched.** mod_php (Apache with PHP loaded in-process) is the highest-risk deployment per PHP's advisory. Distro vendors may backport a fix without bumping the version: confirm with `rpm -q` / `dpkg -l` before closing a finding. A process upgraded on disk but not restarted still shows the old version, which is correct: it is still exposed.

tiles.name: Gaps
tiles.markdown: PHP on hosts without OneAgent (agency-hosted WordPress/Drupal, appliances, ops-tooling boxes). `php-cgi.exe` under IIS that OneAgent did not fingerprint as PHP: check the IIS technology tile and ask the Windows team for `Get-WebHandler` output. IIS sites with a `*.php` handler mapped but idle. Runtime Application Protection does not block this class of bug; Runtime Vulnerability Analytics covers libraries, not the PHP runtime, so this inventory is the source of truth. Exploitation hunting (PHP workers spawning shells) needs exec telemetry such as CrowdStrike Falcon, Falco, Tetragon, auditd, or Sysmon; see the companion notebook.
